metadata.description:
Data for a publication with the title "Lead speed and nepotism in early modern ecclesiastical administration:
A new quantitative approach" published in Historical Methods: A Journal of Quantitative and Interdisciplinary History.

The repository contains CSV results from two queries, as a fallback for a corresponding live SPARQL query against the endpoint, as used in the Jupyter Notebook.

Queries are stored as sq files.

metadata.description:
Documentation

This dataset accompanies the "Critical Online Edition of Eugenio Pacelli's Nunciature Reports (1917-1929)", an open-access digital scholarly edition that critically edits, annotates, and evaluates the diplomatic correspondence of Eugenio Pacelli, later Pope Pius XII, during his service as apostolic nuncio in Munich (1917-1924) and Berlin (1920-1929).

https://pacelli-edition.de/

The documents are exclusively reproduced in the respective original language. The annotation of the documents, biographies and keywords as well as the document's summaries are offered in German throughout.

The project was academically directed by Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. Hubert Wolf and closely integrated into the structure of the Department of Medieval and Modern Church History at the University of Münster. The German Historical Institute Rome (DHIR) provided the technical infrastructure for the Pacelli edition and hosts the project's homepage. The edition was funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) as part of a twelve-year long-term project (2008-2019). 

Dataset Content

The dataset contains the following structured TEI-P5 encoded files:

  • Documents: approximatly 21,000 (TEI-P5).
    • 5,400 final reports sent to the Roman Curia.
    • 5,200 draft versions by Pacelli.
    • 4,200 instructions from curial authorities.
    • 5,200 attachments enclosed in correspondence.
  • Biographies: 5,394 biographical records of referenced persons (TEI-P5).
  • Keywords: 4,544 files of controlled vocabulary and thematic descriptors (TEI-P5).
  • XSLT Stylesheets: Transformation stylesheets used for the display and processing of the edition.
  • XML Schema for validation.
  • Editorial guidelines.

Data Access via API

In addition to this data repository, a REST API is provided to access documents, persons, and topics by ID in XML format (TEI-P5):

  • Document: https://pacelli-edition.de/Dokument/{id}?format=xml

  • Person: https://pacelli-edition.de/Personen/{id}?format=xml

  • Topic: https://pacelli-edition.de/Schlagwort/{id}?format=xml

Example document: https://pacelli-edition.de/Dokument/9032?format=xml

Metadata

All documents, persons, and topics include descriptive metadata in the TEI-Header, ensuring transparency of editorial responsibility, source description, and revision history. The metadata model follows the TEI P5 guidelines and references the Editorial Guidelines: https://pacelli-edition.de/editionsrichtlinien.html.

Authority Data Integration

The edition integrates external authority files such as GND (Gemeinsame Normdatei) and VIAF (Virtual International Authority File). Each person or subject is linked to these identifiers for interoperability and Linked Data compatibility.

        <surname>Beck</surname>
    </persName>
</person>

metadata.description:
This dataset originates from the project GRACEFUL17: Global Governance, Local Dynamics. The transnational Regimes of Grace in the Roman Dataria Apostolica in the 17th century in focus.

It provides information on ecclesiastical offices awarded by the Roman Apostolic Datary, an office of the early-modern Catholic Church. It contain data from dioceses from all over Roman Catholic Europe, focusing on the years 1622/23 and 1677/78. 

Content of this Repo:

Graceful17-Graph-Data.zip

  •  A static data dump of the knowledge graph data provided in N-Triples, N-Quads, TriG, RDF, Turtle (ttl) and JSON-LD format, separated according to the main ontologies used (GRACE, CIDOC CRM, RiC-O).
  • A full dump including all all named graphs (GRACE, CIDOC CRM, RiC-O) in N-Quads and TriG format.
  • All controlled vocabularies and thesauri—e.g. categories of benefices, churches, religious orders, and ecclesiastical provinces—as hierarchically structured taxonomies in SKOS format.

Graceful17-Dioceses.geojson

  • Geodata—in particular for boundaries of dioceses and ecclesiastical provinces—derived from public geospatial sources, primarily the Earthworks project at Stanford University as as GeoJSON.

Graceful17-Transcriptions.tsv

  • Basic transcriptions of the archival sources, along with metadata describing archival storage conditions and creation dates that are provided in Tab-separated Values (TSV) format.

The GRACE ontology used to model the data in the Knowledge Graph is published separately and can be found here.

The Graceful17 knowledge graph can also be queried directly via the SPARQL Enpoint (https://graph.dhi-roma.it/query) or a graphical query builder.

A more detailed description, including the methodological background and instructions on how to query the Knowledge Graph, can be found in the forthcoming data paper.

metadata.title: Libretti of the Music History Department of the German Historical Institute in Rome

description.en: The Creative Commons Attribution license allows re-distribution and re-use of a licensed work on the condition that the creator is appropriately credited.

metadata.description:
Metadat-Set of 1,340 records of the shelfmark group "Rar. Libr." (including the 1,162 libretti from the Giazotto Collection, 655 of which form the holdings of early Venetian prints). A further 200 libretti were donated 2007 and have never been catalogued before. 
Financed by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) and executed in cooperation with the DHI Rome and the Bavarian State Library in Munich, the project aimed at a digitisation of the Music History Department’s Libretti-Collection. In 1979, the DFG had made the acquisition of an anthology of librettos from private collectors possible. Including rare librettos of operas, oratorios, cantatas and festive music from the 17th, 18th and 19th Century, the anthology documents the early phase of public opera in Venice (1637-1734) almost completely. Due to its elevated source value, the libretti inventory is in high demand by library users. Thanks to this project, the libretti holdings have been inserted in the online catalogue of the DHI Rome’s Music History Department and the Virtual Library of Musicology.

metadata.title: Fascism Through the Lense off (Inter)national Newspapers - Poster
metadata.description:
The significant influence that the fascist and National Socialist regimes have had on the national press and publication landscape has been well documented in international research. Nevertheless, the perception and representation of political actions took place not only at home, but also abroad and thus outside the direct sphere of influence of the two regimes. An important example of this is the Digital Exile Press – German-language exile journals 1933–1945 hosted by the German National Library. With the help of quantitative text analyses of the German-language Exile Press and a set of contrastive contemporary German and Italian Press, the corpora will be examined with regard to: 

  • Perception of Fascism and National Socialism from the perspective of the exiled citizens.
  • Reconstruction of media strategies in the political discourse.
  • Characteristic topics of the various press publications.
